brief: Behavior of Current Divergences under SU(3)xSU(3) — Gell-Mann, Oakes & Renner, Phys. Rev. 175, 2195 (1968). The GMOR paper: chiral SU(3)xSU(3) is broken by H' = -u_0 - c u_8, and the pseudoscalar octet masses are pseudo-Goldstone, vanishing with the breaking. m_i^2 = 2 f_i <0|d_mu F_i,mu^5|P_i> (3.4); the per-channel strength W_i(c) (2.10) vanishes for the pion at c = -sqrt(2) but not for kaon or eta, so m_pi -> 0 while m_K, m_eta stay finite. Fitted c ~ -1.25.
extended:
**Behavior of Current Divergences under SU(3)xSU(3)**

*M. Gell-Mann (Caltech), R. J. Oakes (Northwestern), B. Renner (Caltech)* — Physical Review **175**, No. 5, 2195-2199 (25 November 1968). DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.175.2195. Received 22 July 1968. 5 pp.

The paper that fixes the chiral-limit framing of the pseudoscalar meson masses. The SU(3)xSU(3)-violating part of the hadron energy density is assumed to be H' = -u_0 - c u_8 (2.6), with u_0 breaking chiral symmetry but not SU(3) and u_8 breaking SU(3); u_i and v_i are assigned to a single (3,3*)+(3*,3) representation. The axial divergences follow as d_mu F_i,mu^5 = -W_i(c) delta_ik v_k - sqrt(2/3) c delta_i8 v_0 (2.9), with W_i(c) = (sqrt2 + c)/sqrt3 for i=1,2,3 (pion), (sqrt2 - c/2)/sqrt3 for i=4..7 (kaon), (sqrt2 - c)/sqrt3 for i=8 (eta) (2.10). The low-energy vertex gives -lim_{p->0} <P_i(p)|u_0 + c u_8|P_i(p')> = 2 f_i <0|d_mu F_i,mu^5|P_i(p')> = m_i^2 (3.4) — the GMOR relation in the authors' own notation — and its condensate form <0|v_i|P_i> = -m_i^2/(2f_i)W_i(c) ~ -(2f_i)(d_ii0 <0|u_0|0> + d_ii8 <0|u_8|0>) (3.14), with <0|u_8|0> ~ 0 (SU(3)-invariant vacuum) and <0|u_0|0> ~ (3/2)<m^2>_av/(2f)^2.

**Chiral limit.** Abolishing the whole SU(3)xSU(3) violation gives a world with sixteen conserved currents, SU(3) degeneracy and eight massless pseudoscalar mesons (p. 2195); 'the chiral symmetry violation raises the masses of the pseudoscalar mesons to finite values, and the SU(3) violation splits the SU(3) multiplets.' At c = -sqrt(2) the theory has exact SU(2)xSU(2) and m_pi = 0, realized by massless pions rather than parity doubling; the fitted value is c ~ -1.25 (3.12), close to -sqrt(2) ~ -1.414. Breaking runs in two chains, SU(3)xSU(3) -> SU(3) -> SU(2) and SU(3)xSU(3) -> SU(2)xSU(2) -> SU(2) (3.13).

**Why the pion and the kaon differ.** W_i(c) is the only place the channel index enters the axial divergence. At c = -sqrt(2) it vanishes for i=1,2,3 and not for i=4..7 or i=8, so a vanishing pion mass and finite kaon and eta masses are the same statement, not two. The paper also finds f_pi ~ f_K ~ f_eta (3.10) and reproduces the squared-mass (Gell-Mann-Okubo) formula.

**Outline.** I Introduction (p. 2195); II Transformation properties of current divergences (p. 2196); III Applications (p. 2197).
